blocks.text: Inorder emits the complete left subtree, then the node, then the complete right subtree. Under the declared policy `left values ≤ node value ≤ right values`, that local relation composes recursively into a nondecreasing stream; duplicates remain legal when their placement obeys the policy. The traversal needs only the recursive or explicit stack of height `h`. Preorder and postorder preserve useful construction or completion orders but can place a parent on the wrong side of a smaller or larger descendant. Level order groups by depth, which is unrelated to numeric rank. Without the BST precondition, none of these traversals guarantees sorted output, so a sort or another ordered structure would be required.

messages.text: Shallowest-first order reflects depth, not the BST value relation. It is appropriate for per-level or nearest-depth objectives, not for a globally sorted value stream.
Child-first order is useful for subtree aggregates and deletion, but it can emit a right-subtree value before its parent and therefore does not preserve numeric rank.
Parent-first order is useful for prefix serialization and branch pruning, but a parent can precede smaller values in its left subtree.

feedback.reason: The declared BST invariant places every left-subtree value no later than the current value and every right-subtree value no earlier, so left-node-right traversal is the nondecreasing scan.

blocks.text: In an unweighted structure, each BFS layer is one edge farther from the start. Therefore the first matching node dequeued has minimum distance. A proper tree reaches every node through one root path, so visited state is unnecessary. A graph may expose the same vertex through several paths or cycles, so mark identity on enqueue. DFS can compute a minimum after exploring all relevant branches, but its first match is not guaranteed nearest. Postorder deliberately sees deep descendants before their ancestors.

Postorder completion order has no shortest-distance guarantee and may process a deep match before a shallow one. It is appropriate for bottom-up subtree properties, not first-nearest stopping.

items: Tree A, recursive DFS: its height is `Θ(log n)`, so the active root-to-current call chain uses `O(log n)` frames.
Tree A, BFS: a complete tree has a level containing `Θ(n)` nodes, so the frontier queue requires `O(n)` space.
Tree B, recursive DFS: the chain has height `n`, so all `n` frames can be active and space is `O(n)`.
Tree B, BFS: the chain has width one, so processing one node enqueues at most its single child and the queue stays `O(1)`.

blocks.text: Both traversals still take `O(n)` time when each node is processed once. The reusable comparison is `DFS space = O(height)` versus `BFS space = O(maximum width)`; neither traversal has a universally smaller memory bound.

feedback.reason: Recursive DFS stores a root-to-current path, while BFS stores a frontier; height favors DFS on a complete tree and width favors BFS on a chain.

blocks.text: The reader consumes a node token, creates that node, then recursively consumes exactly one left encoding and one right encoding. A null marker is itself a complete empty-subtree encoding, so arbitrary shape remains unambiguous even when values repeat. Inorder values alone do not identify the root of a generic tree, and level-order values without position markers lose gaps. Postorder can support reconstruction when the decoder reads in reverse or buffers children, but that violates the stated forward parent-first contract.

messages.text: Without null-position information, different sparse shapes can produce the same value sequence. BFS serialization can work when it includes explicit missing slots and a finite trimming rule.
Inorder alone does not identify the root or missing child positions for a generic binary tree. It can reconstruct a BST only with extra ordering assumptions and a declared duplicate policy.
The parent token arrives after its children, so a forward-only parent-first reader cannot create the requested object at the required moment. Reverse reading or buffering would change the contract.

feedback.reason: Parent-first streaming requires preorder, and explicit null tokens preserve where each recursive child slot is absent.
